source_span: All eyes are on the 8:30am ET NFP release... investors are increasingly more focused on next week's CPI than the payroll number, given Warsh's assessment of the labor market and Waller's comments yesterday.
source_chain: August NFP is still pending as of this morning (Feroli 50k, Street 55k, prior -23k) therefore it will not by itself settle the September rate debate therefore next Friday's CPI is the real catalyst, with a Fed hold conditioned on core CPI printing +0.1% to +0.2% MoM alongside a ~50k payrolls number; invalidation is a core CPI print outside that range (or an NFP beat well above the 30k-70k 'Goldilocks' band).
pulse_chain: August payrolls printed 162,000 this morning, tripling every bank's forecast and the Street's 55,000, therefore the dovish case built on Waller's mid-week comments is dead therefore the Fed snaps back to pricing a September hike, with the invalidation set at next Friday's core CPI (above +0.2% kills the hold case, inside it keeps the hold alive).
why: The same-day sourcing (JPM, GS, DB Reid) is unanimous that the August NFP had not yet printed as of these morning notes (only previews: GS 40k, DB 65k, JPM/Feroli 50k against a pending 8:30am release), so the pulse's opening premise — an actual 162,000 print 'this morning' that killed the dovish case — is an event none of the day's live notes argue; that figure traces only to an unrelated DB note recapping a stale 'last Friday' release, so the pulse fuses a past, already-known print into today's timeline as breaking news.
